thread.title: Apple Stock Fell on a New Report of iPhone Production Cuts

title: Apple Stock Fell on a New Report of iPhone Production Cuts
text:
Apple Stock Fell on a New Report of iPhone Production Cuts By Updated Nov. 19, 2018 4:23 p.m. ET Order Reprints courtesy of Apple Text size
Apple stock (ticker: AAPL) dropped Monday after a report that the tech giant told its suppliers to cut iPhone production for all three new models.
The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Apple has cut orders in recent weeks for all three newly released iPhone models. The Journal also reported the smartphone maker told several suppliers in the past week that it cut its production plan for the iPhone XR again after an initial reduction in late October, some of the people said. Related Reading Apple Stock Could Keep Falling. Here’s Why
Apple stock closed down 4%, to $185.86. Apple didn’t respond to an emailed request for comment.
Apple’s $749 iPhone XR became available for sale on Oct. 26. The release came after the company put the $999 iPhone XS and the $1,099 iPhone XS Max on the market in September.
Apple stock has fallen more than 15% this month as investors grow increasingly worried about iPhone sales given warnings from suppliers and negative commentary by analysts.
Last week, wireless chip maker Qorvo (QRVO) reduced its financial guidance for its third quarter, citing weaker demand for high-end smartphones. And iPhone suppliers Lumentum Holdings (LITE) and Japan Display (6740.Japan) lowered their financial forecasts on Nov. 12, prompting a selloff in the stocks of Apple and its suppliers.
Earlier this month, the Nikkei Asian Review also reported the tech giant told its suppliers to cancel plans for additional iPhone XR production lines.
